parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
In the following list, underline **all** quantities that are SI base quantities.

charge             electric current             force             time

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Under certain conditions, the distance $s$ moved in a straight line by an object in time $t$ is given by $$s = \frac{1}{2}at^2$$ where $a$ is the acceleration of the object.

State **two** conditions under which the above expression applies to the motion of the object.

parts.label: (c)
parts.part_stem: The variation with time $t$ of the velocity $v$ of a car that is moving in a straight line is shown in Fig. 1.1.
parts.text: Fig. 1.1 [$v / \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ against $t / \mathrm{s}$: at $t = 0$, $v = -10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ rising linearly to $v = 0$ at $t = 4.0\,\mathrm{s}$, to $v = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at $t = 8.0\,\mathrm{s}$, to $v = 20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at $t = 12.0\,\mathrm{s}$, then falling linearly to $v = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at $t = 14.0\,\mathrm{s}$ and to $v = 0$ at $t = 16.0\,\mathrm{s}$.]

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Compare, qualitatively, the acceleration of the car at time $t = 8.0\,\mathrm{s}$ and at time $t = 14.0\,\mathrm{s}$ in terms of:

• magnitude

• direction.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the magnitude of the acceleration of the car at time $t = 4.0\,\mathrm{s}$.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The car is at point X at time $t = 0$.

Determine the magnitude of the displacement of the car from X at time $t = 12.0\,\mathrm{s}$.

marking_points.text: (non-zero magnitude of) acceleration is constant / uniform (and in a straight line)
magnitude of acceleration at $t = 8.0\,\mathrm{s}$ is less than that at $t = 14.0\,\mathrm{s}$
direction of acceleration at $t = 8.0\,\mathrm{s}$ is opposite to that at $t = 14.0\,\mathrm{s}$
